title: Opportunity cost: what you give up when you choose
examples: What does no free lunch mean?

left.label: Football boots
left.ask: How do I make a good choice?

explain.say: Priya has 500 rupees of birthday money. She wants football boots, and she wants a concert ticket, but she can only buy one. Look at the board: a seesaw weighing her two choices.

draw.text: Opportunity cost: what you give up when you choose

left.label: Football boots
left.ask: How do I make a good choice?

explain.say: See the boots side sink lower? That means Priya values the boots more, so she picks them. Choosing is easy when one side is clearly heavier. Which would you choose?

left.label: Football boots
left.ask: How do I make a good choice?

explain.say: Now look at the side that went up: the concert ticket. That is Priya's opportunity cost, which means the next best thing you give up when you choose. It is not the money; it is the thing you missed. What did your last choice cost you?

left.label: Football boots
left.ask: How do I make a good choice?

explain.say: Time has opportunity costs too. Look: an evening of games costs you study time, and an evening of study costs you game time. Neither is wrong; you just weigh them. Which would you pick tonight?

draw.verdict: Every choice gives up the next best one

explain.say: Countries face this too: money spent on a new highway cannot also build hospitals. Wonderful thinking! Wow: economists say there is no such thing as a free lunch, because even free things cost you time.

faq.a: Opportunity cost is the next best thing you give up when you make a choice. If you pick boots over a concert ticket, the concert is your opportunity cost.
No. It is whatever you give up, which can be time, fun, sleep or another item. An hour of TV might cost you an hour of practice.
asks: Can time be an opportunity cost?

faq.q: How do I make a good choice?
faq.a: List your options, think about what each gives you, and compare it with what you would give up. Pick the one whose benefit is worth its opportunity cost.
asks: How do I decide between two things?

faq.a: Yes. Money spent on defence cannot also go to schools or hospitals, so every budget is full of choices about what matters most.

faq.q: What does no free lunch mean?
faq.a: It means nothing is truly free: even a free meal costs your time, or someone else pays for it. Economist Milton Friedman made the phrase famous as a 1975 book title.

facts: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative you give up.
Milton Friedman used There's No Such Thing as a Free Lunch as the title of a 1975 book.

quiz.show: Ama chooses a book over a cinema trip. What is her opportunity cost?
